title: Lease Accounting for Lessees - ASC 842 Complete Guide
learning_objectives: Classify leases as finance or operating
Calculate initial lease liability and ROU asset
Account for lease payments and subsequent measurement
Handle lessee accounting for CPA exam scenarios

cpa_exam_relevance.blueprint_section: Area II - Select Financial Statement Accounts (30-40%)
common_question_types: Journal entries at commencement and subsequent periods

overview.asc_842_changes: ASC 842 (effective 2019-2022) changed lessee accounting by requiring virtually all leases to be recorded on the balance sheet as a right-of-use (ROU) asset and lease liability.
overview.key_model: Single recognition model: All leases create ROU asset and lease liability, but classification as finance or operating affects subsequent measurement and presentation.
overview.scope: Applies to all leases except: short-term leases (12 months or less), leases of intangible assets, leases to explore for or use minerals/oil/natural gas, leases of biological assets

two_types.description: Lessee has substantially all risks and rewards of ownership - similar to purchase
Lessee doesn't have substantially all risks and rewards - true rental

lease_classification.classification_criteria: Finance lease if ANY ONE of five criteria met:

criteria.test: Lease transfers ownership to lessee by end of lease term

criteria.criterion: 2. Purchase option reasonably certain to exercise
criteria.test: Lease contains purchase option that lessee is reasonably certain to exercise

criteria.criterion: 3. Lease term is major part of economic life
criteria.test: Lease term is for major part of remaining economic life of underlying asset
criteria.exception: Don't apply if lease commences at or near end of asset's economic life

criteria.criterion: 4. Present value substantially all of fair value
criteria.test: PV of lease payments equals or exceeds substantially all of fair value of underlying asset
Underlying asset is so specialized it has no alternative use to lessor at end of lease term
criteria.assessment: Asset designed specifically for lessee's needs with no alternative use

lease_classification.default: If NONE of the five criteria met → Operating lease
cpa_exam_tips: Criteria 1 and 2 are YES/NO - no judgment needed
Criteria 3 and 4 have bright-line tests (75%, 90%) - calculate!
Criterion 5 requires judgment about alternative use
Only ONE criterion needs to be met for finance classification

lease_liability.definition: Lessee's obligation to make lease payments
lease_liability.measurement: Present value of lease payments not yet paid, discounted using discount rate at commencement date
lease_payments_included: Variable payments based on index or rate (measured at commencement using index/rate at commencement)
Exercise price of purchase option if reasonably certain to exercise
Penalties for terminating lease if lease term reflects expectation of termination
Amounts probable to be owed under residual value guarantee
For lessees only: Payments for optional renewal periods if reasonably certain to exercise
lease_payments_excluded: Variable payments not based on index/rate (e.g., % of sales) - expense as incurred
Executory costs paid separately to third party (e.g., insurance, taxes, maintenance)

discount_rate.first_choice: Rate implicit in lease (if readily determinable)
discount_rate.definition_implicit: Rate that causes PV of lease payments plus unguaranteed residual value to equal fair value of asset
discount_rate.definition_ibr: Rate lessee would pay to borrow, on collateralized basis over similar term, amount needed to purchase asset

right_of_use_asset.measurement: Lease liability + initial direct costs + prepayments - lease incentives received
components: Lease payments made at or before commencement date (prepayments)
Initial direct costs incurred by lessee
Estimate of costs to dismantle/remove asset or restore site (if obligation exists)
LESS: Lease incentives received from lessor
right_of_use_asset.initial_direct_costs: Costs directly attributable to negotiating and arranging lease that would not have been incurred if lease not obtained (e.g., commissions, legal fees for lease - NOT employee salaries)

facts: Annual payment: $100,000 (paid at end of each year)

lease_liability: Increase liability for interest (using effective interest method)
Decrease liability for lease payments made
rou_asset: Amortize ROU asset (straight-line or other systematic basis over shorter of lease term or useful life if ownership transfers)
income_statement: SEPARATE presentation - like financing a purchase

operating_lease.lease_liability: Same as finance lease - increase for interest, decrease for payments
operating_lease.rou_asset: Amortize to produce straight-line total lease cost over lease term
income_statement: Single lease expense (straight-line over lease term)
operating_lease.calculation_approach: Total lease cost = Lease payments over lease term / Lease term (in periods)

example.facts: Same as initial measurement example, but assume classified as operating
year_1_breakdown: Portion that is interest: $25,274 (same calculation as finance)
ROU asset amortization: $74,726 (plug to get to $100,000 total expense)
example.alternative_entries: Can record as separate interest and amortization components, then reclassify to single lease expense

short_term_lease_exemption.definition: Lease with term of 12 months or less AND does not contain purchase option reasonably certain to exercise
short_term_lease_exemption.accounting_election: Lessee may elect NOT to recognize ROU asset and lease liability
short_term_lease_exemption.if_elected: Recognize lease payments as expense on straight-line basis over lease term
short_term_lease_exemption.scope: Election made by class of underlying asset

components: Periods covered by option to extend if reasonably certain to exercise
Periods covered by option to terminate if reasonably certain NOT to exercise
Periods covered by option to extend (or not terminate) controlled by lessor
reasonably_certain_factors: Economic incentives (significant leasehold improvements, favorable terms)

classification: Only one criterion needed for finance lease
calculations: Don't forget to adjust ROU asset for prepayments/incentives/initial direct costs
Finance lease: separate interest and amortization

key_points: All leases on balance sheet (except short-term election)
Finance vs. operating classification affects income statement and amortization
Lease liability = PV of lease payments at discount rate
Five classification criteria - only one needed for finance
